classification.difficultyReason: Combines regular-polygon angles, isosceles-triangle reasoning, the sine rule and triangle areas to calculate the pentagon's area.

content.prompt: $ABCDE$ is a regular pentagon with side lengths $10\text{ cm}$. Diagonals $AD$ and $AC$ are drawn. Find:

spec.description: Unshaded regular pentagon with A at the top, vertices B through E clockwise, horizontal DC, and diagonals AD and AC. Decorative source blue strokes are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: All five sides are equal; diagonals partition the pentagon into ADE, ADC and ACB. No extra numerical labels, angle arcs or equality marks are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the original pentagon, diagonals and vertex labels are visible.

children.label: b
children.prompt: the area of $\triangle ADE$, correct to two decimal places

answer.worked:
Since $AE=DE$, triangle $ADE$ is isosceles.
$$\begin{align*}\angle EAD&=\frac{180^\circ-108^\circ}{2}\\\angle EAD&=36^\circ.
\end{align*}$$
Using the sine rule:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AD}{\sin108^\circ}&=\frac{10}{\sin36^\circ}\\AD&=\frac{10\sin108^\circ}{\sin36^\circ}\\AD&\approx16.18\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

The base angles of isosceles triangle $ADE$ are equal.
$$\begin{align*}\angle ADE&=\frac{180^\circ-108^\circ}{2}\\\angle ADE&=36^\circ.\end{align*}$$

The pentagon's interior angle at $D$ is $108^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle ADC&=108^\circ-36^\circ\\\angle ADC&=72^\circ.\end{align*}$$

Triangles $ADE$ and $ABC$ are congruent by SAS, so $AD=AC$. Hence triangle $ADC$ has equal base angles.
$$\begin{align*}\angle DAC&=180^\circ-72^\circ-72^\circ\\\angle DAC&=36^\circ.\end{align*}$$

children.label: g
children.prompt: the area of $\triangle ADC$, correct to two decimal places

answer.worked:
Use the unrounded diagonal length $AD=AC=\dfrac{10\sin108^\circ}{\sin36^\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of }\triangle ADC&=\frac12(AD)(AC)\sin36^\circ\\\text{Area of }\triangle ADC&=\frac12\left(\frac{10\sin108^\circ}{\sin36^\circ}\right)^2\sin36^\circ\\\text{Area of }\triangle ADC&\approx76.94\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$

children.label: h
children.prompt: the area of the pentagon, correct to two decimal places

answer.short:
$172.05\text{ cm}^2$

Add the areas of the three triangles, retaining unrounded intermediate values.
answer.worked:
Congruent triangles $ADE$ and $ABC$ have equal areas. Retain unrounded areas from parts b and g.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of pentagon}&=2\times\text{Area of }\triangle ADE+\text{Area of }\triangle ADC\\\text{Area of pentagon}&=2\left(50\sin108^\circ\right)+\frac12\left(\frac{10\sin108^\circ}{\sin36^\circ}\right)^2\sin36^\circ\\\text{Area of pentagon}&\approx172.05\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
